headword: {鉄筋|てっきん}コンクリート
reading: てっきんこんくりーと

definitions.explanation: Concrete strengthened with steel bars or mesh embedded within it. The standard construction material for buildings and infrastructure in Japan.

examples.japanese: この{建物|たてもの}は{鉄筋|てっきん}コンクリート{造|づく}りだ。
examples.english: This building is made of reinforced concrete.

examples.japanese: {鉄筋|てっきん}コンクリートの{建物|たてもの}は{耐震性|たいしんせい}が{高|たか}い。
examples.english: Reinforced concrete buildings have high earthquake resistance.

examples.japanese: {築|ちく}{三十年|さんじゅうねん}の{鉄筋|てっきん}コンクリートのマンションに{住|す}んでいる。
examples.english: I live in a thirty-year-old reinforced concrete apartment building.

notes:
USAGE:
Often abbreviated as RC ({鉄筋|てっきん}コンクリートの{略|りゃく}) in real estate listings and construction documents. Appears frequently in apartment and housing descriptions.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {鉄筋|てっきん}コンクリート{造|づく}り (reinforced concrete construction)
- {鉄筋|てっきん}コンクリートの{建物|たてもの} (reinforced concrete building)
- RC{造|ぞう} (RC construction — abbreviated form)

RELATED WORDS:
- {鉄骨|てっこつ}: steel frame
- {木造|もくぞう}: wooden construction
- {耐震|たいしん}: earthquake-resistant
